page: Microsoft Azure D4alds_v6 is a virtual machine instance from the Daldv6 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The instance is configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with multithreading enabled. It includes 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Local storage is bundled with a 236 GB disk, and the instance is capable of utilizing Premium Storage.

Benchmark data reveals strong single-core performance, with the stress-ng single-core CPU test scoring 3079.18 and the Geekbench single-core test reaching 2078.0. However, multi-core scaling and memory performance present notable constraints. The Geekbench multi-core score is average at 4740.0, and memory bandwidth is weak, measuring 37.74 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 303.96 GB/sec for cached small-block reads. This memory bottleneck impacts memory-intensive operations, as reflected in the weak Passmark memory score of 1746.14 and the weak Redis SET performance of 5.88 million operations per second.

Given the 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and the bundled 236 GB local storage, this instance is positioned as a compute-oriented option with low memory allocation. It is suitable for single-threaded tasks, basic web serving, and lightweight text processing. It is poorly suited for memory-heavy databases, software compilation, or medium-to-large language model inference, where prompt processing for a 7B model drops to a poor 11.78 tokens per second. The hardware profile offers a cost-efficient entry point for compute-bound workloads that do not require large memory footprints.
